clauses.current_legal_basis: The order's own held text (42 FR 58509) has no end and the bounded searches found no later instrument. The held text of 38 U.S.C. 3680 (release point 119-121 through 2026-10-09) authorizes in subsection (a)(2)(A) continued allowances during temporary closures under an established policy based on an Executive order of the President, capped at 4 weeks in any 12-month period, and prints this order in its Executive Documents note. Checked through 2026-10-14.
clauses.reason: Section 1 allows the Administrator of Veterans' Affairs to continue monthly educational assistance benefits when an institution plans to close between semesters or terms for not more than 45 days because of energy conservation, once in any 12-month period per institution; section 2 requires advice to beneficiaries about their entitlement period. Nothing in the text ends it. The authority cited (former section 1780(a), now 38 U.S.C. 3680(a)) is in force, and subsection (a)(2)(A) of the held statute now covers closures under an established policy based on an Executive order, so the clause continues, operating within the statute's current 4-week cap and with the function stated for the Secretary of Veterans Affairs. Those statutory changes narrow how the clause is exercised; they do not end it.

research_rationale:
Read the whole order (42 FR 58509, signed 1977-11-08): section 1 lets the Administrator of Veterans' Affairs continue monthly educational assistance when an institution closes between terms for not more than 45 days to conserve energy, exercisable once in any 12-month period per institution; section 2 requires the Administrator to advise beneficiaries of the effect on their entitlement. The order has no own-terms end. Held current law: the text of 38 U.S.C. 3680 (release point 119-121 through 2026-10-09) now provides in subsection (a)(2)(A) that the Secretary may continue allowances while institutions are temporarily closed under an established policy based on an Executive order of the President or due to an emergency, capped at 4 weeks in any 12-month period, and its note prints this order. The three bounded searches were read against their coverage notes; current-law:usc hits the note, current-law:ecfr and later-events:ofr_catalog have no hit beyond the order. Authority statute checked in force: clause (A) of former section 1780(a), now 38 U.S.C. 3680(a), is in the held text. The 4-week statutory cap and the statute's use of the Secretary are changes made by statute to the underlying authority, not later presidential instruments, and are disclosed in the clause reason.

savings.reason: The order has no saving clause. Allowances already paid under it before any change in the statute are outside any held source. No instrument restoring or ending the policy was found by the three bounded searches, so the state is none after bounded search.
